newsitem.title: MALAWI: MALAWI CIVIL SERVANTS SUSPEND SIX-WEEK STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: MALAWI CIVIL SERVANTS SUSPEND SIX-WEEK STRIKE.

text.p: Malawi civil servants on Tuesday suspended their six-week strike for higher wages and said they would return to work afer progress in talks with the government, a union leader said.
Civil Servants Trade Union leader Thomas Banda told national radio civil servants would be briefed on Wednesday to return to work after progress in weekend wage negotiations.
"The six-week industrial action has been suspended. The ground work for talks has been cleared smoothly," Banda said.
Government workers are demanding a 100 percent pay rise recommended by an independent commission two years ago.
Banda said the government had agreed to reinstate all dismissed workers except those who committed crimes during the strike.

The Malawi government is refusing to grant the 100,000 civil servants the 100 percent increase, saying it would destabilise the economy, which grew by more than nine percent in 1996 and is projected to grow seven percent this year.
It has offered to increase wages by 47 percent. Malawi's lowest-paid workers earn on average $20 per month.
